decision: Primary target is Sales; Customers is a secondary target with its own model.
reason: Dashboard needs both outputs; Customers is not in test.csv, so it cannot feed the sales model.

decision: Main forecast horizon is 42 days; the same pipeline covers the 48-day test window.
reason: Brief asks for six weeks ahead; test.csv spans 48 days.

decision: Final holdout = last 42 labelled days of train, scored once after all choices are locked.
reason: Gives an honest estimate of forecast error; test.csv has no Sales to score against.

decision: Three earlier rolling 42-day validation windows with common cut-offs across stores.
reason: Tests stability across time without touching the final holdout.

decision: Model log1p(Sales); loss = RMSE on the log scale; primary metric = RMSPE on positive-sales days; MAE and RMSE secondary.
reason: Sales is right-skewed and finance cares about percentage error; log RMSE behaves like relative error.

decision: Predict zero when a store is closed; train on open days only.
reason: All closed days have zero sales; including them would distort the model.

decision: Do not cap Sales with IQR rules; treat outliers only with evidence from store histories.
reason: High sales may be genuine holiday or promotion peaks the model must learn.

decision: No actual future Customers or Sales may be used as forecast inputs; history is allowed only before the forecast origin.
reason: Prevents leakage; Customers is not available in test.csv.

decision: Use a shared LSTM across stores (store and calendar inputs) as the main deep learning design.
reason: More practical than 1,115 separate models and runs in Colab.

decision: Build the app with Streamlit and host it on a free platform.
reason: Brief allows Streamlit; free hosting is sufficient for the project.

decision: Unit tests, CI/CD and Docker are optional; list as pending if skipped.
reason: Not required by the brief; avoid claiming work that was not done.

decision: Settings (paths, seed 42, horizon, tracking names) live in src/config.py; one logger and one style module are shared by notebook and app.
reason: A single source of truth keeps results, figures and the app consistent.

decision: MLflow uses a local SQLite store (mlflow.db); models are logged as pickles (cloudpickle); trial run kept in a separate 'setup-check' experiment.
reason: Supports the model registry and multiple model versions; pickles match the brief's .pkl requirement.

decision: DVC tracks the whole data/ folder as one unit with tagged versions (data-v1-raw, v2-cleaned, v3-features); the local store path is kept out of Git.
reason: The history of one pointer file shows multiple data versions for the DVC screenshot.

decision: Two requirements files: requirements.txt (app only) and requirements-dev.txt (notebook and tracking).
reason: Keeps hosting installs small and fast while the notebook stays fully reproducible.

decision: Figures are saved as 'Figure <section>.<n>' in figures/ and tables as 'Table <section>.<n>' in outputs/tables/, all in the shared palette.
reason: Notebook, report and slides can cite the same numbered items.

decision: Models will be saved as dd-mm-yyyy-HH-MM-SS.pkl using config.MODEL_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT.
reason: Matches the brief and lets predictions be traced to a model.

decision: A minimal Streamlit page is deployed early as an environment check.
reason: Finds hosting and dependency problems before the final week.
status: Provisional (confirm once the hosted check passes)

decision: Read StateHoliday as text and keep codes 0, a, b, c.
reason: Avoids treating numeric 0 and text '0' as different categories.

decision: Keep every store-day (nothing deleted). Open days with zero sales are flagged (suspect_zero_sales) and excluded from training through use_for_training.
reason: Refines D06: the rows look like recording errors, but keeping them avoids creating new date gaps.

decision: Stores missing a long block of days are flagged (has_history_gap, missing_history_days); sequence and rolling features must not cross the gap.
reason: The same block is missing for every affected store and filling it would invent sales.

decision: Missing test Open values are set by the rule 'open unless Sunday or state holiday' and flagged (Open_imputed).
reason: Evidence from the same store in train supports the rule.

decision: Competition distance: median plus flag. Competitor opening dates: unknown stays unknown (flagged); years before 1990 treated as unknown.
reason: Avoids inventing competition ages; distance is a store attribute with no sales information.

decision: Promo2 details are coded as not applicable (None / 0) for stores that do not participate.
reason: The missing values are structural, not unknown.

decision: Unusual sales are flagged with a store-by-weekday robust z-score (|z| > 5) and kept; no IQR capping.
reason: A global IQR rule would remove promotion peaks and large stores; flagged rows can be tested in a sensitivity run in Section 7.

decision: Cleaned tables are saved to data/interim as train_clean, test_clean and store_clean (compressed CSV) and versioned in DVC as data-v2-cleaned.
reason: Later sections start from one agreed cleaned dataset.

decision: Final holdout = 20 Jun 2015 to 31 Jul 2015 (42 days). It is locked in code (get_masks) and every use must be written to the evaluation-access log.
reason: Gives one honest score on history never used for tuning; test.csv has no sales.

decision: Three rolling validation windows of 42 days before the holdout: rolling_1 14 Feb 2015 to 27 Mar 2015; rolling_2 28 Mar 2015 to 08 May 2015; rolling_3 09 May 2015 to 19 Jun 2015. Each window trains on all history before it (expanding window) and is forecast from one cut-off shared by all stores.
reason: Tests stability over time and matches how the real forecast will be made.

decision: Seasonal stress test: 01 Aug 2014 to 17 Sep 2014 (48 days, 935 stores with complete history). Reported alongside the rolling windows, not used for tuning.
reason: It is the only window that resembles the test window (summer school holidays about 43% vs 44%); it also covers forecast days 43 to 48.

decision: Feature-availability policy enforced in code (src/validation.py): only known-future, store-static and origin-history features are allowed as inputs; Customers and cleaning controls are blocked. Engineered features must be registered with a class.
reason: Makes leakage a failed check, not a judgement call.

decision: No fitting of any kind (scalers, imputers, encoders, aggregates, models) on rows after a split's training end date.
reason: Prevents information from the forecast window entering the model.

decision: In validation windows, Open, Promo and holiday columns use their actual values, as if the plans were known in advance.
reason: The real test file supplies the same planned fields, so this mirrors how the forecast will be used.

decision: History features are computed at forecast origins (training rows built from several past origins, each looking back only from its own origin). Lag features are only allowed in a clearly labelled recursive simulation that never uses actual validation sales.
reason: Keeps training rows consistent with how forecasts are produced.

decision: The final model is refit on all labelled history only after every choice is locked.
reason: Section 10 handles the final refit and the single holdout scoring.

decision: All exploration uses only the development period (up to the day before the final holdout).
reason: Keeps the locked holdout unseen, even in aggregate figures.

decision: Comparisons use a 'sales index' (a day's sales divided by the store's typical sales on that weekday) and 'ordinary days' (no state holiday); promotion effects compare Monday-to-Friday days only.
reason: Makes big and small stores comparable and removes weekday and holiday mix as an explanation.

decision: Promotion effects are reported as associations on a chain-wide alternating-week calendar; competitor-opening effects use stores with complete history, comparison stores and a placebo test.
reason: No experiment exists, so claims stay descriptive.

decision: Q7 (opening and closing times), the city-centre part of Q10 and the 'missing distance becomes known' part of Q11 are reported as not answerable from the supplied data.
reason: The data has no hourly detail, no location and no time dimension in store.csv.

decision: Candidate features carried to Section 6: weekday x promotion, promotion-week position, days to and from Easter, Christmas and national holidays, school holidays, December run-up, 24 December, days since reopening after a closure, Sunday-trading flag, store type, assortment, competitor distance bands, months since a competitor opened and its distance.
reason: Each is supported by a finding in this section; Customers cannot be used (not available in test).
status: Confirmed (built in Section 6; see the feature catalogue)

decision: Training rows are built from forecast origins every 28 days plus the start of each validation window; each origin creates rows for the next 48 days, and only targets inside the development period are kept.
reason: Training rows then look exactly like the real forecast: one cut-off, planned inputs for the future days, history only up to the cut-off. Targets stay out of the locked holdout.

decision: The feature set has 61 features in three availability classes: known-future, store details and history up to the origin. Customers, sales on forecast days and the cleaning columns are never inputs; the raw store number is not used.
reason: Enforced by the availability policy; store scale comes from history features instead of an arbitrary store ID.

decision: Holiday-distance features use only holidays flagged for at least 90% of stores in the data, capped at 30 days. Regional holidays and holidays after the last date in the files are not invented.
reason: Source documented: the StateHoliday flags in train.csv and test.csv.

decision: An unknown competitor opening date is counted as an established competitor (24 months) with the 'date known' flag kept; a competitor opening after the date gets its own flag.
reason: Avoids inventing recent openings; the flag lets a model see the difference.

decision: Preprocessing is one ColumnTransformer: numeric features get median fill, a missing-value flag and StandardScaler; category features get most-frequent fill and one-hot encoding with unknown categories ignored; yes/no flags pass through unscaled. It is fitted on training rows only and reused unchanged for validation, test and the app.
reason: Same transformation in training and inference; scaling helps distance-based and neural models.

decision: Same-weekday and same-week sales from one year earlier are included as optional features.
reason: Possible store-specific seasonality, but missing for the first year and for stores with the 2014 gap; an ablation in Section 7 decides whether they stay.

decision: History features come from open days with positive sales only, and are computed separately for every forecast origin.
reason: Closed days and suspect zero-sales rows would distort a store's level.

decision: The feature tables are saved to data/processed and versioned in DVC as data-v3-features.
reason: Models in Sections 7 to 10 start from one agreed feature table.

decision: Models learn log(1 + Sales) with squared error and are scored by RMSPE on positive-sales days (MAE and RMSE as secondary metrics). Closed days are forecast as 0; open days with zero sales are not scored.
reason: On the same model, the log target gave an RMSPE 5% lower than raw sales and far lower than weighting raw sales by 1/sales squared; finance cares about percentage error.

decision: Success target fixed after measuring the baselines: average rolling RMSPE of at most 0.13 and a better score than the best baseline (Store-by-weekday-and-promotion average) in every window. Result with 150,000 training rows: 0.1297.
reason: A concrete bar that is neither trivial nor tuned to the models; the full-data refit in Section 10 decides whether it is met.
status: Met on the final holdout (Section 10.2): RMSPE 0.1068

decision: Tuning protocol: 13 configurations (Ridge 4, Random Forest 3, gradient boosting 6 sampled at random), each fitted on 100,000 rows in the three rolling windows, selected by the lowest average rolling RMSPE. The seasonal check was never used for tuning.
reason: A documented, affordable budget that keeps the seasonal check an independent test.

decision: Every model is an sklearn pipeline (preprocessing, estimator) wrapped so it learns log(1 + Sales) and predicts Sales; each is registered in MLflow (rossmann-ridge, rossmann-random-forest, rossmann-gradient-boosting).
reason: One object per model that can be saved, served and called on a table of features.

decision: Finalist: Gradient boosting with min_samples_leaf=20, max_leaf_nodes=127, max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, l2_regularization=0.0.
reason: Lowest error in every window (rolling and seasonal check), small (4 MB), fast to score; Random Forest is 131 MB and less accurate; Ridge cannot beat the promotion-aware baseline.

decision: The same-year-earlier features are dropped, leaving 59 features.
reason: Removing them changed the rolling error by only 0.75%, and they are missing for the 180 stores with the 2014 gap; the simpler pipeline is easier to serve.
status: Confirmed in Part 2 (R.2): -0.68% at 400,000 rows, within the 0.5% rule (at 150,000 rows the rule had kept them: +0.76%)

decision: Flagged unusual sales stay in the training data.
reason: Removing unusually low sales raised the rolling error by 4.6% and removing all flagged rows by 3.0%.

decision: The final model is trained on all labelled history rows (Section 10).
reason: On rolling window 3, error fell from 0.116 with 50,000 rows to 0.102 with 800,000 rows.

decision: The chain-level series is the average sales per open store per day over the development period (900 days). One typical store of each type is isolated as well (the store closest to its type's median, among stores with a complete history).
reason: An average per open store is not distorted by closures or by the 180 stores missing from 2014; typical stores show how the pattern looks at store level.

decision: Stationarity: ADF rejects a unit root (p < 0.0001) and KPSS rejects level stationarity but accepts trend stationarity, so the series is trend-stationary. Differencing is not needed for stationarity; lag-1 and lag-7 differences raise the variance, while a two-week difference lowers it to 0.86 of the original.
reason: The levels are kept for the main LSTM; a two-week-differenced variant is tested in 8.3 and adopted only if it helps.

decision: The dominant cycle is two weeks, not one: autocorrelation peaks at lags 14 and 28, and the cycle strength is 0.60 for a 14-day period against 0.36 for 7 days. Input windows must cover at least 28 days and the model needs the planned promotion calendar as an input.
reason: Promotions alternate weekly, so the sales rhythm repeats every two weeks.

decision: Differencing is carried out and reversed with src/timeseries.py (difference_chain and invert_chain), and the reversal is verified to be exact.
reason: A model trained on differenced data must turn its forecasts back into sales.

decision: Final feature set after re-applying the Section 7 rule at 400,000 rows: 59 features (without) (59 features).
reason: Removing the same-year-earlier features changed the average rolling RMSPE by -0.68% (rule: drop only if at most +0.5%). D53 had recorded a drop that the Section 7 code did not make (Table 7.20 and MLflow version 2 use 61 features).

decision: LSTM samples use a direct 48-day strategy: 56-day history window, a training origin every 7 days anchored at the latest origin whose targets fit in the training period, planned inputs for every future day, (-1, 1) range scaling fitted on training days only (store level: log sales minus the store mean), lazy windows cut from one panel (src/sequences.py).
reason: Matches the real forecast (one cut-off, a long window, a known calendar); five leakage and correctness tests pass.

decision: Days missing from the record (the 2014 gap) are zero-filled and flagged with has_record; a history window needs records on at least half of its days; nothing is interpolated.
reason: Keeps the 180 gap stores usable soon after the gap without inventing sales.

decision: Deep learning framework: Keras 3.15.1 on tensorflow (code uses keras.ops only, so the PyTorch backend also works); seeds via keras.utils.set_random_seed.
reason: Colab default; portable to Python versions without a TensorFlow build.

decision: Decision rule for 8.5 (fixed before scoring): gradient boosting stays unless a challenger (store LSTM or 50/50 LSTM + GB average) wins every rolling window and the seasonal check, has a pooled-rolling bootstrap 95% interval below zero, and improves RMSPE by at least 3%.
reason: Prevents choosing a model on noise and accounts for the extra serving cost of an LSTM.

decision: Direct 48-day forecasting is used for the store-level LSTM. At chain level, recursive and direct forecasts are close: average rolling RMSPE 0.0845 (recursive) vs 0.0832 (direct); seasonal check 0.0714 vs 0.0682.
reason: Neither framing wins clearly (differences are of the size of the seed spread). Direct forecasting needs one pass per origin instead of 48 sequential ones, cannot feed its own errors back, and reads the planned calendar of every future day directly, so it is kept.

decision: History window: 56 days kept (rolling-average chain RMSPE: 28 days 0.0807, 56 days 0.0832, 84 days 0.0833; best = 28).
reason: 56 days covers four two-week cycles; differences between windows are compared with the seed spread before changing the design.

decision: Two-week differencing is not adopted (chain RMSPE 0.2117 differenced vs 0.0832 levels); per-day head kept (flat head 0.2647).
reason: 8.1 showed the series is trend-stationary; differencing is only worth its extra inversion step if it lowers the error.

decision: Model going forward: Gradient boosting. Pooled rolling RMSPE: gradient boosting 0.1334, store LSTM 0.1529, 50/50 ensemble 0.1370, best baseline 0.1741.
reason: Decision rule D64 applied as fixed before the comparison.

decision: Customers are forecast by a separate gradient-boosting pipeline on the same 59 features (faster learning (rate 0.1)); target log1p(Customers).
reason: Average rolling RMSPE 0.1088 against 0.1480 for the customer baseline.

decision: Explanations use three measures (split gain, time-aware permutation, SHAP); the largest feature group by SHAP is 'History: store level' (47%).
reason: Different measures answer different questions; agreement between them is reported, not assumed.

decision: Prediction intervals: conformal by forecast week and store size, nominal 90%, calibrated on all three rolling windows for the app; days 43 to 48 use week 6.
reason: Calibrated on rolling 1 and 2 it covered 90.3% on rolling 3 and 90.0% on the seasonal check; chosen because it is closest to 90% both overall and in its worst store-size group (quantile regression covered only 82.7%).

reason: Average rolling RMSPE 0.1088 against 0.1480 for the customer baseline.
